content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposes to use the standard GPT-3 for a specific, important task, which is producing humoristic dialogues. 
Target language is Chinese and the target corpus is based on the  Chinese Comical Crosstalk. Crosstalk scripts
are challenging as these are: 1) multiple-turn; 2) humor-oriented; 3) with a novel language style; 4) culturally-grounded
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- a novel interesting corpus is presented 
- a first analysis of the existing method is carried out

Weaknesses:
- results are rather weak
- no novel methods are presented
- no insight into results is given
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper focuses on the novel dataset, which is extensively presented. The motivations of the study are clear.  Hence, the novelty is in the corpus and in the idea of reproducing comical crosstalk by using text generators such as GPT and others.

There are some minor remarks:
-language use is odd sometimes, e.g.:
     Solving this problem "algorithmically" requires deep semantic understanding --- what algorithmically means here?
     preventing it from ____extermination____.???
     We also manually reviewed some ___advertising___ words???
     maintained as shown in ___Listing 9___???
- citations in text have the wrong format , e.g. Mutton et al. (2007) should be (Mutton et al., 2007) if the citation does not play a grammatical role in the sentence
content.summary_of_the_review:
The main focus of the paper is the creation of the dataset, yet, it is not clear how this datset has been produced:
1) has it been obtained from internet? If this is the case, why it should be digitalized?
2) how the sharing 80% of characters has been computed? With a bag-of-characters? With a blue score?
3) Most importantly, Human calibration. The procedure is not fully  described. How many annotators? What are the guidelines? What does it mean: scripts without sense?
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes to test if current NLG models can generate humor. Specifically:

* It presents a data set of Chinese comical crosstalk scripts. 
* It benchmarks various NLG models.

The authors conclude that all NLG models, even the large PLMs are far from generating good humor.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

* This paper looks at C3/humor, which has not yet been investigated in our community.
* It benchmarks not only the most popular large-scale PLMs but also the smaller ones.
* The authors made an effort to address the ethical issues with C3.

Weaknesses:

* The evaluation metrics are out of date. BLEU was also never a good metric, to begin with.
* Since humor is less researched in our field, I was hoping to see a more subjective/human evaluation to compensate for the less suitable automatic ones.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is relatively clear, with some insights but not enough. Since the authors will be releasing their code and their data, it should be fairly easy to replicate.
content.summary_of_the_review: This is a novel paper looking at interest phenomena. I am leaning towards rejection but would strongly encourage the authors to dig deeper and come back.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a new dataset consisting of digitized Chinese Comical Crosstalk scripts. The paper formulates two new tasks for the proposed dataset: a seq2seq utterance generation task and a next-word generation task. The proposed cross talks have four distinct characteristics. The paper cleans, preprocesses, and calibrates the data. The paper benchmarked four kinds of different baselines on the new dataset. The paper evaluates the generation quality both automatically and manually.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The paper proposes a new Chinese Comical Crosstalk dataset and two new tasks. The proposed dataset is exciting and valuable for future research. The paper shows detailed statistics of the proposed dataset. The paper gathers the dataset from multiple resources with preprocessing. The paper also provides potential ethical issues related to the dataset, which can benefit future users.

2. The paper tests four major kinds of natural language generation baselines on the dataset. The baselines include most state-of-the-art models such as GPT3 and Pangu-$\alpha$. The paper provides a detailed analysis of the automatic evaluation results. The paper did a qualitative analysis of those baselines in the case study. In addition to the automatic evaluation, the paper also conducts a human evaluation to check further aspects that are not covered in the automatic metrics, such as humor, general quality, ethics, etc. The paper includes potential future research directions in the discussion section. 

Weaknesses:
1. Some parts of the paper can be improved, which will be discussed in the clarity section.

2. The paper can include more automatic evaluation metrics instead of simple token overlap-based metrics such as BLEU and ROUGE. The paper needs to include some newer metrics such as BERTscore (Zhang et al., 2019), and BARTScore (Yuan et al., 2021) which can check semantic similarity. 

Zhang, T., Kishore, V., Wu, F., Weinberger, K. Q., & Artzi, Y. (2019). Bertscore: Evaluating text generation with bert. arXiv preprint arXiv:1904.09675.

Yuan, W., Neubig, G., & Liu, P. (2021). Bartscore: Evaluating generated text as text generation. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 34, 27263-27277.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. Some parts of the paper can be improved. For example, for the second task(next word generation), it might be better to formulate it as a pertaining step instead of a task because the results for the next step generation are not shown in the paper. The dataset statistics such as train/valid/test split might be better put in the Appendix instead of on the attached Github page. The paper might attach more generation results in the appendix. Some parts of the human assessment are unclear such as the number of annotators. The font size of Table 6 is a little bit small. 

2. The paper provides an anonymous GitHub link that provides training details, dataset statistics, and some models for reproduction. The paper also provides their human evaluation interface and other training details in the Appendix. The paper also provides potential ethical issues in section 4.3.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, the paper proposes a very interesting dataset along with tasks. The paper benchmarked state-of-the-art models on the dataset and did both automatic and human evaluations.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors of this paper study the problem of humor generation by comparing various approaches on a new dataset of digitized Chinese Comical Crosstalk scripts that has been collected. The authors trained multiple models on the new dataset and used various automated metrics to compare the performance on the new task. Results indicate that GPT3 performs the best on automated metrics.

Contributions:
1. A new dataset for humor generation in the Chinese Language.
2. Demonstrating that using large scale pre-training improves crosstalk generation quality and scripts generated
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength and Weakness:
1. Creation of a new Chinese dataset for crosstalk from digitized Chinese comics which is valuable to the community. However, this does raise issues if the authors have the rights to collect and open source this dataset especially scraping it from book and other websites?
2. One of the issues as highlighted with this dataset is the ethical issues and bias present in the collected scripts. It would have been great a significant addition to the paper if the authors would have demonstrated the steps they have taken to tackle those problems instead of just mentioning them briefly.
3. The authors do a good job of comparing various approaches on this dataset. Results from the automated metrics show that the GPT3 performs the best on most of the metrics but automated metrics do not do a good job is capturing the performance of the model.
4. Human evaluation shows that GPT3 achieves the best on the metric of general quality and humor and coherence. What is the definition of the metric of "general quality", " humor degree", "coherence" and "ethically risky"? Why is the kappa agreement so low amongst the annotators? With such a low agreement, how do we know that the human evaluation is not filled with noise?
Comments:
1. Typo in Page 4 "number of performers" section. It should be "sketch" instead of "ketch"
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The main originality of the work comes from the dataset work. From the approach and technicality perspective, originality is quite limited and this work just compares existing approaches on new datasets without any significant contribution.
content.summary_of_the_review: In this work, the authors collect a new dataset for chinese cross talk from digitized scripts and compare the performance of various existing approaches on the new dataset.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.
